label: Benchmarking
definition: Systematic comparison of computational tools on standardized datasets to evaluate accuracy, scalability, and reproducibility.

label: Cell-free DNA
definition: Analysis of fragmented extracellular DNA circulating in plasma or other body fluids, with applications including prenatal testing, transplant monitoring, and cancer liquid biopsy.

label: CRISPR
definition: Experimental and computational topics related to CRISPR-Cas systems, including genome editing, gene regulation, base editing, guide RNA design, and pooled functional screens.

label: Deep learning
definition: Machine learning subfield using multi-layer neural network architectures to learn hierarchical representations from biological data, with applications in sequence analysis, image analysis, and structure prediction.

label: Differential expression
definition: Statistical identification of genes or transcripts whose abundance differs significantly between biological conditions or cell populations.

label: Gene set analysis
definition: Statistical methods testing whether predefined sets of biologically related genes are enriched for differential activity in a genomic dataset.

label: Genome annotation
definition: Computational identification and labeling of structural and functional elements in a genome sequence, including genes, non-coding RNAs, regulatory regions, and repetitive elements.

label: Genome graph
definition: Graph-based data structures encoding multiple genome sequences and their variation, enabling alignment, variant calling, and haplotype-aware analysis beyond a single linear reference genome.

label: Immune repertoire
definition: High-throughput sequencing and analysis of T-cell receptor (TCR) and B-cell receptor (BCR) diversity generated by V(D)J recombination.

label: Liquid biopsy
definition: Non-invasive sampling of tumor-derived material circulating in blood or body fluids, including ctDNA and circulating tumor cells, for cancer detection, monitoring, and treatment assessment.

label: Long-read transcriptomics
definition: RNA sequencing using long-read platforms to characterize full-length transcript isoforms, novel splice junctions, fusion transcripts, and RNA modifications.

label: Microbiome
definition: The collective genetic content, taxonomic composition, and functional potential of microbial communities, studied to understand host-microbe interactions and community dynamics.

label: Nanopore sequencing
definition: Oxford Nanopore sequencing technology that detects bases from ionic current disruptions as molecules pass through nanopores, producing ultra-long reads and enabling direct RNA sequencing and base modification detection.

label: Pangenomics
definition: Study of the complete set of genomic sequences across multiple individuals or strains, typically represented as a graph capturing variation absent from a single linear reference genome.

label: Protein language models
definition: Transformer-based deep learning models pre-trained on protein sequences to learn co-evolutionary patterns, enabling prediction of function, stability, mutational effects, and structure.

label: Single-cell multiomics
definition: Simultaneous or joint measurement of two or more molecular modalities from individual cells, such as gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and surface protein.

label: Spatial transcriptomics
definition: Transcriptomic profiling that retains the physical coordinates of gene expression within a tissue section, linking molecular data to histological context.

label: Tumor microenvironment
definition: The ecosystem of non-cancerous cells, extracellular matrix, and signaling molecules that surround tumor cells, studied to understand immunosuppression and treatment response.

label: Variant annotation
definition: Computational annotation of genetic variants with predicted functional consequences, allele frequencies, disease associations, and regulatory context.

label: Variant effect prediction
definition: Computational prediction of the molecular and phenotypic impact of genetic variants, including missense pathogenicity, splicing disruption, and regulatory element effects.
